title: Security pen test results + SDLC & patching cadence review - Summit Bank
next_steps: Redwood to share sanitized pen-test report and remediation plan link by 2026-04-23
Customer to provide list of required compliance artifacts (SOC2 controls mapping) by 2026-04-28
Schedule follow-up deep dive on KMS integration with Summit Bank HSM on 2026-04-30
action_items: Ethan Cole - Upload sanitized pen test report, remediation plan and IOCs to shared link - due 2026-04-23
Ravi Menon - Send Summit's required evidence list and compliance checklist - due 2026-04-28
Maya Patel - Prepare pricing/contract addendum for dedicated/managed HSM option - due 2026-05-04
summary: Redwood and Summit Bank reviewed results from recent pen test, discussed triage and remediation timelines, alignment on vulnerability management and secure SDLC practices, and next steps for KMS/HSM integration and audit evidence for SOC2.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Ravi (Summit Head of Security), Laura (Summit CTO), Diego (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we just wanna run through the pen test that landed last week and go over patching cadence, vuln mgmt, sdlc questions. Ethan will run the findings.
[00:18] Ravi: Yep thanks. we got the report, a few high/mediums and some infoals, curious about remediation timeline and how you guys handle exposed configs in dedicated vs hosted.
[00:30] Ethan: yeah, hi all. quick note: the report we've shared is sanitized, there are a few IOCs that we took out for safety, full details in the secure link. Link: https://redwood.internal/secure/pen-test-summit (note: placeholder)
[00:45] Laura: quick Q before deep dive, does remediation require changes to our VPC peering or customer-managed keys? we have strict HSM requirements.
[00:59] Ethan: great q. short answer: depends on the finding. for cryptography we've recommended optional HSM integration for KMS-bound keys - that's the managed HSM offering. most fixes are config/patches to runtime images and dependency upgrades, not infra rework.
[01:15] Diego: can you clarify the 'token leakage' note? the report flagged an example where a log line contained a partial token.
[01:26] Ethan: right, so that was an info/low severity; caused by debug logging left on in one service. we have log redaction in the platform, but in that customer-configured path debug was enabled; fix is to disable debug by default and apply log redaction rules - we've pushed a patch that prevents raw tokens from being emitted in logs.
[01:44] Ravi: are those redaction changes already rolled out to hosted? what about Dedicated and Private?
[01:51] Ethan: hosted already has the patch in canary, rolling to prod next week. Dedicated customers get the same remediation but we ship a patch bundle that you can apply; for Private (on-prem) we provide the patch and a short runbook to apply, or we can assist under support contract.
[02:10] Laura: ok - what about SSO/SSO sessions? the pen test flagged session fixation in an older session library - has that been updated?
[02:20] Ethan: yes that's a medium finding tied to an older session lib. we've upgraded the dependency and recompiled the runtime. will push an advisory and version hash in the shared doc. For Dedicated instances we'll coordinate a rolling restart window.
[02:36] Ravi: on vuln mgmt more broadly, what's your cadence for vulnerability scanning and patching? we usually require monthly patch windows and a documented SLA for CVE triage.
[02:48] Maya: we've had a monthly cadence for dependency scanning and weekly infra scans; critical/high CVEs have an accelerated track - 48-72 hours for remediations or mitigations. we can map that to Summit's policy but need to confirm the SLA in contract.
[03:05] Diego: do you integrate with our ticketing (Jira) for automatic ticket creation for findings?
[03:10] Ethan: we support webhook integrations and can create Jira tickets automatically; we'll show the integration in the follow-up runbook.
[03:19] Ravi: thanks. there were two medium findings re: RBAC misconfig and overly permissive service account. can you walk the mitigation?
[03:28] Ethan: sure. those were caused by default role binding in a cluster template that didn't follow least privilege. mitigation: rotate keys, create least-priv roles, apply auditing, and we added hardened templates. Also we now enforce a policy via OPA/rego in CI to block broad bindings.
[03:48] Laura: are those OPA checks part of your CI? can we see the policy as part of the artifact set for SOC2 evidence?
[03:56] Ethan: yes, policies and audit logs are available. we'll package them as part of the SOC2 evidence bundle; note though for Private deployments some artifacts are customer-provided or deployed inside your network so we provide signed statements and runbooks.
[04:15] Ravi: on audit logs, we need logs to be immutable and retained for at least 1 year, preferably 3 for some controls. what's current retention?
[04:25] Maya: default retention is 90 days for hosted, with extended retention add-on up to three years. For Dedicated we can configure longer retention; for Private you'd control retention in your storage. we do offer S3-compatible export and time-stamped signed digest for immutability.
[04:44] Diego: any E2E encryption in transit and at rest? where does KMS factor in?
[04:50] Ethan: data in transit TLS 1.3, at rest we encrypt payloads and cache on disk. Keys are in Redwood KMS by default; we support customer-managed KMS with HSM (bring-your-own-HSM) for Dedicated/Private. Integration notes and policy for key rotation are in the KMS integration doc.
[05:08] Ravi: sample question: does Redwood retain prompt+response for hosted by default and what's the opt-out? we require no retention for certain regulated flows.
[05:18] Maya: default is short-term retention for telemetry and debugging; customers can opt out of storing prompt/response with a per-route config and opt-in to strict non-retention. we also support data residency controls by region.
[05:29] Laura: ok good. returning to pen test: the two high findings were around container escape in an outdated runtime and a path traversal in an auxiliary service. what's the remediation ETA?
[05:41] Ethan: container escape vector - we've rebuilt the runtime with patched base images and hardened seccomp and AppArmor profiles. fix scheduled in hosted within 72 hours; for Dedicated we'll coordinate a patch window. path traversal - library upgrade and input validation; PR merged, will be in the next release.
[06:02] Ravi: will you provide CVSS scores and proof of fix (hashes, build artifacts)?
[06:07] Ethan: yes, we'll include CVSS, commit SHAs, container image hashes, and a short verification checklist in the remediation report we upload.
[06:18] Diego: any automated regression tests to ensure these fixes don't break latency SLAs?
[06:24] Ethan: our CI runs perf regression tests; we also run sampling traces against canary to measure token-latency and throughput; if we see >10% degradation we hold rollout.
[06:36] Ravi: about secure SDLC do you do threat modeling and PR-level security reviews?
[06:43] Maya: our engineering org requires threat modeling for new services, PR-level security checks, SCA (software compose analysis), and automated SAST/DAST scans in the pipeline. We can provide the policy and evidence artifact for SOC2.
[06:58] Laura: do you track developer access to secrets? we've strict controls and ephemeral creds only.
[07:04] Ethan: we use vault for secrets and ephemeral creds for infra; access is RBAC enforced and logged. Admin actions require MFA and approval workflows. logs are forwarded to SIEM.
[07:17] Ravi: good. another question: patch cadence for third-party libs  you said monthly, but for critical CVEs is that a 48-hour response? is that contractual?
[07:27] Maya: currently operational policy is 48-72h for critical; we can negotiate contractual SLA if Summit requires it as part of Dedicated or an enterprise support tier.
[07:37] Diego: for Dedicated/private customers can we get schedule for patch windows to align with our release calendar?
[07:43] Ethan: yes we can schedule maintenance windows and rolling restarts to minimize impact. We'll propose times in the next email.
[07:55] Ravi: about pen test scope was the test against hosted endpoints or dedicated? we need to confirm that any issue in hosted doesn't leak into our Dedicated instance.
[08:06] Ethan: testers had access to a sandboxed hosted environment that was configured to mimic a typical tenant but no direct access to customer Dedicated infra. cross-tenant impact was not observed, but we included isolation checks in the report.
[08:22] Laura: are there any findings that require data residency changes? like logs crossing regions?
[08:30] Ethan: we flagged one audit log export configuration that would have sent logs to a central bucket in another region  that's a misconfig for that sandbox; default for production is region-bound, and for Summit we'll restrict exports to your region.
[08:46] Ravi: ok. can you outline the remediation timeline for high/medium/low? we need that for our risk register.
[08:55] Ethan: High: within 72h for hosted fixes and coordinated patch window for Dedicated/Private; Medium: 2 weeks for full remediation or mitigation; Low: in the next quarterly rollout. We'll produce a triage matrix.
[09:12] Diego: what about CVE disclosure cadence? will you notify customers and share mitigation steps?
[09:18] Maya: yes we send security advisories and a customer notification for high/critical CVEs, and we publish mitigation steps in the support portal. We can add Summit to priority distribution.
[09:31] Ravi: do you maintain an incident runbook for suspected compromise including forensics and notification timelines?
[09:38] Ethan: yes, our IR runbook is 3 phases: detect, contain, remediate, and notify. SLA for initial notification is within 4 hours of confirmed incidents for enterprise customers.
[09:52] Laura: for SOC2 evidence, we need to see change control, deployment logs, and signed audit logs. Can you provide a pack?
[09:59] Maya: yes we'll assemble a SOC2 evidence bundle with change control docs, build artifact hashes, CI logs, and the audit log digests. for Dedicated we can provide signed attestations.
[10:12] Ravi: one more ops question: do you do pentest remediation verification tests (re-test) or do we need to run our own follow-up test?
[10:20] Ethan: we offer a re-test for high/critical fixes as a complementary courtesy within the engagement window; for extended assurance we recommend a third-party re-test which we can coordinate.
[10:31] Diego: any blockers for Summit to onboard Dedicated with HSM? what's the timeline to provision?
[10:38] Maya: provisioning Dedicated with customer-managed HSM typically takes 4-6 weeks including procurement and networking. If Summit wants accelerated setup we can prioritize but need contract for dedicated capacity and support.
[10:51] Ravi: cost question: is HSM add-on billed separately?
[10:55] Maya: yes HSM and extended retention are add-ons; we'll include pricing in the follow-up deck.
[11:03] Laura: perfect. let's recap next steps.
[11:07] Maya: recap: Ethan will upload sanitized pen test report + remediation matrix + hashes by 2026-04-23; Ravi will send evidence/control list by 2026-04-28; we schedule KMS/HSM deep dive on 2026-04-30; Maya to send pricing/contract addendum by 2026-05-04.
[11:25] Ravi: thanks, that works.
[11:28] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the secure link.
[11:33] Laura: thanks all.

End of transcript.
